A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLaRA work. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical formulation, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original VIMA-Bench evaluations, ablations, and real-world robot experiments under zero-shot, finetuning, and joint-training protocols.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline evaluations, prompt-sensitivity results, and quantitative real-world generalization tests.

M1.justification: The LLaVA-based policy, image-coordinate action representation, inBC/D-inBC conversion, six auxiliary tasks, action history, and multi-step planning remain unchanged. Action prediction and planning details emphasized in v2 already appear in v1's figures and Appendix A.1.

E1.justification: V2 adds testing with ten unseen complex rephrasings of real-world task instructions. VIMA and xArm coverage otherwise remain stable: distractors and the weighing-and-return task already appear in v1's Figures 11–12. Using all 660k VIMA trajectories expands training volume, rather than establishing new task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 introduces and evaluates D-RT-2 Style (I), which encodes image-coordinate actions with special tokens, providing an important control for the natural-language formulation. It also expands the VIMA comparison to include RT-2-style baselines trained on the full dataset (Table 9), substantially strengthening the comparator design.

E3.justification: New experiments train RT-2-style baselines on all 660k VIMA trajectories for one through four epochs (Table 20). Appendix B.7 adds random, absent, and fifteen fixed inference-prompt conditions, while Section 6.2 adds explicit zero-shot/finetuned generalization evaluations. These extend the evaluation design; retained experiments keep their existing metrics and settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds a systematic action-prompt sensitivity study (Appendix B.7, Figure 13) and quantitative robustness tests involving distractors, complex rephrasing, and weighing-and-return behavior (Table 4). Existing auxiliary-data, action-history, planning, multiple-image, and detector ablations are retained. The longer-training analysis already existed and is extended with the new comparator.

E5.justification: V2 first explicitly reports twenty randomly initialized real-world episodes per setting. Simulation evaluation retains twenty random seeds, now described as per task. This is additional reporting, not evidence of increased repetition; neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched existing numerical results retain their values. V2 adds image-coordinate baseline results, full-VIMA baseline results, and prompt-sensitivity measurements. Its new Table 4 reports distractor/rephrasing/weighing success rates of 10/0/0% zero-shot and 75/40/20% after finetuning. These substantially extend the empirical record rather than show same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The MDP, demonstration-dataset, and history-conditioned policy formulations are unchanged. Neither version adds substantive theorems, proofs, derivations, or formal guarantees; revised notation and action-space explanations do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The contribution list replaces the scalable-data-pipeline contribution with image-coordinate action alignment for data-efficient transfer, which the conclusion also emphasizes. The claim of requiring no external data is narrowed to requiring no extra action labels or task/action supervision. The central policy-learning and auxiliary-data claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 more explicitly attributes auxiliary-data gains to information rather than additional optimization steps, extending v1's underfitting discussion. Section 6.2 interprets the new tests as preserved generalization after tuning. Limitations more specifically associate textual-description and detector constraints with additional reference images; the main noise and 3D-movement limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 specifies cosine scheduling, a 0.03 warm-up ratio, maximum learning rate of 2e-5, xArm7/Logitech C140 hardware, and cropping from 640×480 to 640×320. It also clarifies baseline action encoding. These are newly documented details, without evidence that retained experiments changed; the code/data/model access statement already existed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds SpatialVLM and sequence-model/self-supervised-learning references and develops explicit distinctions from PaLM-E and SpatialVLM. It removes the designation of 3D-VLA as the closest work while retaining its citation. These refine positioning around direct action generation and auxiliary supervision without replacing the overall research framing.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites and reorganizes the narrative: related-work discussions are consolidated, method subsections become compact thematic paragraphs, auxiliary-task descriptions are paired, and real-world details move into a dedicated appendix. The expanded experiments gain numbered subsections, and a reproducibility statement is added.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the overview, merges v1's Figures 6–7, relocates training curves and qualitative examples, and adds robot-setup and prompt-sensitivity figures. It expands comparison tables and adds generalization/full-data tables, alongside widespread layout and table-format changes. Relocated results remain available in the appendices.

improvement.justification: The coordinate-matched token baseline and full-data RT-2-style experiments address important gaps in v1's evidence for its action formulation and data efficiency (Appendices A.4 and B.2). Quantitative generalization tests make previously anecdotal capabilities assessable, while implementation disclosures improve reproducibility. Some new generalization language exceeds what the 40% rephrasing and 20% weighing results justify, but the stronger controls and more transparent evidence provide a substantial net improvement.
